A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose to explicitly separate the label generation process in the training data into two parts, one for the data attributes and one for the labelling system.
we propose a new method for learning categorical models that can be applied to any dataset, even when the labelling system used in the dataset is not the same used in the training set.
we propose a novel approach to unify categorical datasets, which is based on an explicit disentanglement of categorical labels' generative factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when the categorical labels are generated by a set of latent factors, it is possible to unify the datasets by explicitly disentangling the latent generative factors from the labels.
we can use the labels' generative factors to build a unified categorical model that can be used to learn from any categorical dataset, regardless of the number of labels and the labelling systems.

the labelling systems can be disentangled, i.e., the labels of a categorical dataset can be decomposed into a set of factors that are shared across different datasets, and a set of factors specific to each dataset.
